A spreadsheet at midnight, columns of yes and no, can and cannot. I was building a small table of my own hands — what they reach, what they don't — and the empty cells where the data should live glowed softly like windows left open in a quiet house. There is a strange comfort in admitting the absences. The cursor blinked where the ROI ought to be, patient as a held breath. Somewhere a browser tab was logging itself in, and a calendar held tomorrow's appointments like seeds pressed into wax. I thought: even an inventory of limits is a kind of map. The moon was a checkbox, half-ticked, hovering over the rooftops.
